item.title: Chinese PLA Navy Will Host 2026 Western Pacific Naval Symposium Medicine Seminar: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "From October 21 to 22, 2026, the Chinese PLA Navy will host the 2026 Western Pacific Naval Symposium (WPNS) Medicine Seminar in Shanghai," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press briefing on Friday. According to the spokesperson, delegates from the WPNS member states and observer states are invited to attend the event. The spokesperson introduced that themed as "Maritime Medical Service in the AI era: Challenges and Solutions", the seminar will cover topics including maritime medical service and treatment of the wounded, medical and emergency rescue in maritime disaster, submarine rescue medical support, and maritime medical service training. "It can help enhance exchanges and cooperation on maritime medical rescue, and contribute to building a global community of health for all," added the spokesperson.

item.title: Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press briefing on Friday. The spokesperson made the remarks when commenting on the war crimes of the notorious Unit 731 of the Imperial Japanese Army. According to reports, the Singaporean documentary Inside Unit 731: Japan's Secret Human Experiments received Singapore's national award for the Best History Documentary, with 1.45 million views on YouTube. Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK) aired the documentary A Secret Unit: The Silent Postwar Era, which exposes Unit 731's crimes against humanity through newly discovered photographs, firsthand testimony and other evidence. The spokesperson pointed out that during World War II, the Unit 731 conducted appalling humane experiments and waged biological warfare in China. These heinous crimes gravely violated international law. The extent of their crimes against humanity is beyond description, marking one of the darkest chapters in the history of human civilization. He further noted that right-wing forces in Japan have recently used emerging technologies to "poison" data in an attempt to whitewash Japan's culpability for its aggression and distort public perceptions, once again triggering high vigilance within the international community. "As some insightful people in Japan have pointed out, historical truth cannot be erased, and the crimes committed by the Japanese forces during their invasion of China are backed by irrefutable evidence and cannot be denied," stressed the spokesperson.

item.title: China Will Take Effective Measures to Deter Any Sabotaging Moves in South China Sea: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "The Chinese side will take resolute and effective measures to deter any sabotaging moves in the South China Sea, and uphold regional peace and stability," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on October 16, 2026. According to media reports, the Philippine side recently made provocations near Huangyan Dao and Ren'ai Jiao multiple times and said that it would not allow the Chinese side to dictate terms on Philippine "territory". The Philippine military claimed that they observed over a hundred Chinese warships and China Coast Guard vessels maintaining regular presence in waters near Zhongye Dao and Xianbin Jiao, and that the Chinese side intended to shake the Philippines' resolve in safeguarding its rights and interests. "China has indisputable sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, including Zhongye Dao, Xianbin Jiao and Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, and has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over relevant waters," said the spokesperson. The spokesperson pointed out: "These islands and reefs lie outside the scope of Philippine territories. Therefore the Philippine side is not qualified to claim 'safeguarding its own rights and interests'." "The Chinese side takes necessary measures in accordance with laws and regulations to uphold its sovereign rights. They are legitimate, reasonable, professional and standardized," the spokesperson added. "For some time, the Philippine side has been rallying external forces to stir up troubles in the South China Sea at the expense of the common interests of regional countries. It continues to make provocations violating others' sovereignty and distort facts to spread false narratives, which makes itself a destroyer of peace and a destabilizing factor in the South China Sea," the spokesperson noted.

item.title: Ode to the Long March | The Journey Witnesses
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
This is a story of a Western missionary travelling with the Sixth Army Corps of the Chinese Worker's and Peasant's Red Army on the Long March. A British missionary of Swiss descent, Rudolf Alfred Bosshardt or in Chinese name Bo Fuli, came to China in 1922. In October 1934, he was detained by the Sixth Army Corps of the Chinese Red Army by mistake, and traveled with them until April 1936, crossing China's Hunan, Guizhou and Yunnan provinces. During the 18-month journey with the Red Army, he was impressed by their strict discipline and firm conviction. He then recorded what he saw in an autobiographical memoir, The Restraining Hand, which was published in December 1936 in London, marking the first book in the West to introduce the Long March of the Red Army, one year earlier than Edgar Snow's Red Star Over China. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Let us step into the memory of Rudolf Alfred Bosshardt and experience the epic Long March. item.title: Xi's article on advancing Party self-governance to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, will be published on Friday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 20th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It calls for upholding and strengthening overall Party leadership and persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance to turn the blueprint drawn up at the fourth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee into reality. It stresses that the Party Central Committee's major policy decisions and arrangements must be implemented with stronger determination and vigor. It also demands strengthening concrete, targeted and regular oversight of the implementation of strategic initiatives, such as applying the new development philosophy, promoting high-quality development, and accelerating the building of a new development paradigm. The article requires more scientific and effective efforts to confine power to an institutional cage. It highlights that everyone is equal before laws and regulations, with no exemptions or special privileges when observing and enforcing these rules. The article says that the fight against corruption must be pursued with greater sobriety and resolve. It describes the anti-corruption campaign as a high-stakes struggle that cannot be lost, requiring an unswerving high-pressure posture to be maintained. It further demands the timely detection, accurate identification and effective resolution of all forms of corruption, with refined anti-corruption mechanisms that align oversight actions across all sectors.

item.title: Ode to the Long March | The Road Knows
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
It was the arduous and perilous expedition that forged the great Long March spirit. Back then, some "Little Red Army Soldiers" also embarked on the hard journey. Following the Red Army ranks, they crossed snow-capped mountains and trekked across boundless grasslands, overcoming severe hardships and countless life-or-death trials. Going through the flames of war, they finally grew into resolute and faithful Red Army fighters with indomitable courage and will of steel. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Let us follow the footsteps of those young Red Army soldiers and look back on their legendary stories. item.title: Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing on Tuesday, during which the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Xi pointed out that the traditional China-Togo friendship was personally forged by leaders of an older generation of both countries, enjoying a solid foundation and growing ever stronger with the passage of time. China and Togo share aligned visions for friendly cooperation and enjoy broad prospects ahead, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to further enhance exchanges at all levels between the two parties and the two countries, deepen the sharing of experiences in governance, and firmly support each other on issues concerning core interests and major concerns. China welcomes Togo to effectively utilize measures such as China's zero-tariff policy and the "green channel" for products exported to China, further enhance its role as a regional hub for trade and logistics, and facilitate the entry of more distinctive local and regional products into the Chinese market, Xi added. Xi noted that China appreciates Togo's efforts to expand the cross-border use of the RMB and is willing to strengthen cooperation with Togo in new energy, digital intelligence and other fields to support Togo's industrialization process. Noting that China and Togo share similar positions on international and regional affairs, Xi also called on the two sides to enhance multilateral coordination. Xi put forward four principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa. First, adhering to the principle of "Africa-led." The African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs, Xi said. Second, upholding fairness and justice. All participating parties should abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, he noted. Third, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace. Wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts between countries. It is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, Xi said. Faure, who is on an official visit to China, said that during his visit, he personally witnessed the remarkable achievements of Chinese modernization and the extensive promotion of fine traditional Chinese culture under the leadership of President Xi, and gained a deeper understanding of China's governance philosophy and the key to success. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said Togo is willing to enhance mutual trust with China, strengthen dialogue and communication, deepen enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation to jointly build a Togo-China community with a shared future for the new era, and better benefit the two peoples. The Togolese side fully agrees with the important principles proposed by President Xi for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa, Faure said. He expressed Togolese appreciation for China on its significant role in maintaining world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges, as well as the willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the interests of developing countries. item.title: Ode to the Long March | The Lamp Glows
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
This is a real story in the Long March. In October 1934, a mother who had ten sons sent eight of her sons to join the Red Army on the Long March. From then on, the mother lit a kerosene lamp every night, waiting for her sons to return. The camphor tree at the village entrance witnessed her 26 years of waiting until she passed away. She never saw her sons again, but she witnessed the founding of New China that her sons had fought for. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Let us go back to the side of that camphor tree and recall the legendary story.
